Holy Shotgun Print Kit

A display prop modelled on the crucifix shotgun from Constantine, broken into parts that print without supports on a 220 mm bed. It cannot fire anything: the barrel is a hollow sleeve over a solid rod and the shells are solid dummies.

  • 581 x 224 x 238 mm assembled
  • 21 printed part types
  • 34 printed pieces
  • about 700 g of filament

    What you need besides filament

    • 8 mm rod, about 640 mm in total: 345 mm for the barrel spine, 203 mm for the cross arms and 90 mm for the drum axle. Aluminium tube, steel rod or a hardwood dowel all work.
    • 8 M3 x 30 socket head screws for the receiver, grip tongue and trigger. They thread straight into the plastic.
    • 3 M3 x 20 socket head screws for the grip halves.
    • Super glue or epoxy for the barrel joints, torch, sight and Dragon's Breath tube.

    Print settings

    • 0.4 mm nozzle, 0.2 mm layers, 3 walls, 15% infill. PLA or PETG.
    • Every STL is already turned the way it should sit on the bed. No supports.
    • Use a brim on the tall, thin parts: the rear barrel sleeve, the torch and above all the twisted rod.
    • Two colours cover it: brass for everything except the drum, recoil shield, shells and trigger, which are silver.

    Assembly order

    1. Screw the two grip halves together with the M3 x 20 screws.
    2. Glue the rear drum flange onto the hex spigot of the drum core. Push the 90 mm axle through the drum and slip the recoil shield onto the axle behind it, tab at the top.
    3. Lay the right receiver half on the table, outer face down. Drop in the grip tongue and the trigger, then lower the drum, axle and shield in together. Lay the rear end of the 345 mm spine rod in its groove.
    4. Close the left receiver half over it and drive in the eight M3 x 30 screws from the right side. The drum should spin freely.
    5. Slide the rear barrel sleeve down the spine rod onto the receiver, then the cross hub. Push the 203 mm rod through the hub and slide an arm and its cap onto each side. Finish the spine with the front sleeve and the muzzle cap. Glue each joint as you go.
    6. Glue the pedestal to the top of the rear sleeve, 76 mm ahead of the receiver, and set the torch in it with the bell facing forward. Glue the cross sight into its slot at the muzzle.
    7. Push the twisted rod into the socket at the front of the receiver. Glue the small saddle onto the Dragon's Breath tube, then offer the tube up under the hub and slide it back onto the rod. Glue the saddle to the hub.
    8. Load the twelve shells through the gate on the right side of the recoil shield.

    Two cautions

    • The layout and proportions follow photos of the film prop, but nothing was measured from the original. The dense hand engraving is reduced to scrollwork on the grip, a few crosses and three inscriptions, and the trigger is fixed. Every dimension is a named parameter in model.py.
    • It still looks like a firearm from a distance. Print the muzzle cap in blaze orange or paint the tip, and carry it in a bag outside the house.
